records.title: Dashboard data is generated, not committed
records.context: Browsers block a page opened from disk from reading neighbouring JSON files, and a committed bundle would conflict on every merge.
records.decision: The CLI writes .repostate/data.js after each change; it is gitignored. Git hooks rebuild it after pulls, and the page can also load the folder through a file picker.
records.consequences: A fresh clone needs one build (or the hooks) before the dashboard shows data.
records.author: noreply@anthropic.com

records.title: One JSON file per type, one record per line
records.context: One file per record produced hundreds of small files (one per test case), which cluttered the repo and every commit.
records.decision: Each type is one file, .repostate/<scope>/<type>.json, with one record per line sorted by id. A git merge driver, enabled by the hooks command, merges two branches record by record.
records.consequences: A handful of files instead of hundreds. Without the merge driver, two branches adding records to the same file can conflict like any text file. Folders from before 0.3 are still read and are converted by init.
records.author: noreply@anthropic.com

records.title: One JSON file per record instead of one tasks.json
records.context: Several people and agents edit the same repo on different branches. A single file conflicts on almost every merge.
records.decision: Each record is its own file at .repostate/<scope>/<type>/<id>.json, with random ids so two branches never create the same id.
records.consequences: Merges only conflict when two people edit the same record. Listing needs a folder scan, which is fast at repo scale.
alternatives: JSONL with a custom merge driver
records.after: one JSON file per record, written by the CLI
records.author: noreply@anthropic.com

records.title: Team data committed, personal data gitignored
records.context: Teams need shared visibility; individuals need scratch space and per-branch reviews that should not land in main.
records.decision: team/ is committed; personal/ and config.local.json are gitignored. promote and unshare move records between them. Reviews and notes default to personal.
records.consequences: Everyone with repo access sees team data, and access follows repo permissions. Personal data stays on one machine.
records.author: noreply@anthropic.com

records.title: JSON files in git, not SQLite
records.context: The dashboard must open as a static file with no server, data must diff and merge in git, and it must follow branches and worktrees.
records.decision: Store records as JSON. Revisit a SQLite cache only if a repo grows past tens of thousands of records.
records.consequences: Readable diffs and no binary files in git. Queries scan files, which is fine at expected sizes.
records.author: noreply@anthropic.com
